name: The Forward Deployed Tester
techName: src/agents/forward-deployed-tester/ — crawler.ts · locators.ts · findings.ts · generators.ts · report.ts · index.ts
oneLiner: Point it at a running web app; it crawls, records findings and provisions a complete Playwright + MCP test project in one run.
lead: A new engagement starts and there is no test estate. This agent does the first week in one run: it launches a real Chromium through Playwright, walks every same-origin page it can reach from `target_url`, harvests the accessibility tree, writes severity-graded findings to the shared SQLite database, and leaves behind a runnable Playwright + Playwright MCP project — page objects, a smoke suite, a `consoleErrors` fixture, CI, a README and `.mcp.json` — plus `report.md` and `report.json`. In the 2026-09-11 04:32 run against a local three-page demo site it rendered 3 pages in 2.0 s, recorded 4 findings (2 medium, 2 low), derived 9 locators of which 8 are role-based, and wrote 11 files. It needs no model: with `LLM_PROVIDER=none` every deliverable is identical, and a local open-weight model only rewrites the executive summary. In the engagement described on the [process page](../process.html) this is the surface probe of the Discover phase.
chore: Someone spends the first week clicking through the app, pasting URLs into a spreadsheet, hand-writing a `playwright.config.ts` from a blog post, inventing page objects with brittle CSS selectors, and wiring a CI workflow nobody trusts. Meanwhile the obvious defects — a 404 in the footer, a form nobody can tab through, a console full of red — go unrecorded because "we are still setting up".
instead: One command. A crawl table per page (status, load time, console errors, failed requests, counts, h1, landmark), findings by severity with evidence JSON, a locator inventory with a confidence per element, a project you can `npm test` on the first run, and a report you can hand to the client — all traceable to a run id in the database.
whyItMatters: The thesis behind this repo is that vendors' forward-deployed engineers deliver the AI and nobody independently measures what they delivered. Measurement needs a deterministic regression layer that exists **before** the pilot starts. This agent makes that layer exist on day one, from the running app alone, with no credentials beyond what a browser needs.

howItWorks.step: Validates the request with a zod schema: a URL, an org slug, and defaults for the page budget (15), the per-navigation timeout (15 s), headless mode and MCP output; optional basic-auth credentials or session cookies.
howItWorks.explain: The runner calls `agent.inputSchema.parse(rawInput)` before a run row exists, so a bad request never creates a run. `max_pages` is capped at 50 and counts **rendered** pages only; broken links do not consume the budget. `auth` is a discriminated union: `basic` becomes Playwright `httpCredentials`, `cookie` becomes `context.addCookies` with `path: '/'`. The schema applies defaults, which is why its input type is wider than `Input` and the definition casts it — the contract only ever calls `.parse()`.

howItWorks.step: Normalises the start URL, fixes the origin, and walks a breadth-first queue: every rendered page's links are normalised, deduplicated and admitted only when they are same-origin and not an asset.
howItWorks.explain: `normaliseUrl` drops the hash and a trailing slash so `/about/` and `/about#top` are one queue entry. `isCrawlable` rejects other origins and anything whose path ends in an asset extension (images, css, js, pdf, docx …). Two budgets bound the loop: `maxPages` for rendered pages and `maxPages + 100` for total visits, so a site with hundreds of dead links still terminates; everything left in the queue is reported as `skipped`. The browser is closed in `finally`, so a crash mid-crawl cannot leak a Chromium process. The 2026-09-11 run made 4 visits: 3 pages rendered, 1 broken, 0 skipped, 1986 ms.

howItWorks.step: Visits one URL with listeners for console errors, uncaught page errors and 4xx/5xx responses, waits for `load` and then up to 2 s of network idle, and runs the harvest script inside the page.
howItWorks.explain: A response with status ≥ 400 returns `{ broken }` and never reaches the harvest, so a custom 404 page is not catalogued as a page. A thrown navigation error (DNS, timeout, TLS) becomes `broken` with `status: 0` and the first line of the error. The `response` listener skips the page's own URL so a 404 page is counted once, as a broken link, not twice. The network-idle wait is capped at `min(2000, timeout)` and its rejection is swallowed: a page that never goes idle still gets harvested. Listeners are removed in `finally` so errors from page N do not leak into page N+1.

howItWorks.step: Harvests the DOM in the browser as plain JavaScript: accessible names via `aria-labelledby`, `aria-label`, `<label for>`, a wrapping `<label>`, then value / alt / title / placeholder; counts unlabeled controls and the forms that contain them, images without `alt`, the `<h1>` and landmark regions; caps at 60 visible interactive elements per page.
howItWorks.explain: This is a `String.raw` template, not a TypeScript function, on purpose: a TS function passed to `page.evaluate` gets transpiler helpers such as esbuild's `__name` injected, which do not exist inside the page. `isVisible` drops `hidden`, `aria-hidden`, `display:none`, `visibility:hidden` and zero-rect elements, so page objects only get things a user can reach. `accName` is a practical subset of the accessible-name computation, in the same precedence order. Test ids are read from `data-testid`, `data-test-id`, `data-test` and `data-cy`. "Unlabeled" means no label, no `aria-label`, no `aria-labelledby`, no placeholder and no title — the same conditions under which `getByLabel()` cannot target the control.

howItWorks.step: Picks a Playwright locator per element in Playwright's own priority order — role + accessible name, label, placeholder, text, test id — and only then CSS by id, `name` attribute, stable classes or tag, each with a confidence.
howItWorks.explain: `implicitRole` maps common HTML to ARIA roles (a `<a href>` is a `link`, `<input type=email>` a `textbox`, `<select>` a `combobox`), so most elements get `getByRole(role, { name, exact: true })` at high confidence without any test ids. `looksGenerated` refuses ids and classes that look like framework output (`ember123`, `css-1x2y3z`, `:r1:`, hashes, long digit runs), which is why the demo's `<input name="first">` — no label, no placeholder — fell through to `page.locator("input[name=\"first\"]")` at **medium** confidence while the labelled email field became `getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email" })` at **high**. A role without a name is emitted at low confidence only when nothing else identifies the element; a page where half the elements end up low gets an `info` testability finding.

howItWorks.step: Turns the crawl into findings with fixed severities: navigation failures and 5xx are high; 4xx links, console errors, slow pages over 3 s and forms with unlabeled controls are medium; missing alt text, no `<h1>` and no landmark are low; a mostly untargetable page is info; nothing rendered at all is critical.
howItWorks.explain: Pure function: crawl in, drafts out. `index.ts` persists each draft with `ctx.db.addFinding` and then reads the rows back, so the report shows database ids and the same counts the REST API returns. Severity is decided per category, never by a model. `SLOW_PAGE_MS` is 3000; three times that is high. Evidence is stored as JSON next to the row (the broken link record, the console text, the counts), so a finding can be re-checked without re-crawling.

howItWorks.step: Provisions the project as pure strings — `package.json`, a `playwright.config.ts` with three desktop and two mobile projects, a `consoleErrors` fixture, one smoke test per page, one page object per page, README, GitHub Actions workflow, `.gitignore` and `.mcp.json` — and registers every file as an artifact.
howItWorks.explain: Class names come from the path (`/` → `HomePage`, `/about-us` → `AboutUsPage`) and are made unique with a numeric suffix. Each smoke test navigates through the page object, asserts the response is below 400, the title matches, the `<h1>` contains the harvested text (or leaves a `NOTE` when recon found none — as it did on `/about`), and that the `consoleErrors` fixture collected nothing. Page-object getters carry a doc comment with tag, type, role, strategy and confidence so a reviewer can find the low-confidence ones with a grep. All of this is unit-tested without a browser: `tests/forward-deployed-tester/generators.test.ts` renders the files from in-memory page records.

howItWorks.step: Writes `report.md` and `report.json` with an executive summary that is deterministic by default and only rewritten by a local model when one answers — and kept only if the rewrite is between 40 and 1200 characters.
howItWorks.explain: `maybeLlm(fn, fallback)` resolves the provider once per process (`auto` probes Ollama on 127.0.0.1:11434, then an OpenAI-compatible server on 127.0.0.1:8080, then `none`), returns the fallback when nothing answers, and also returns the fallback if `fn` throws. The prompt forbids new facts and demands every number be kept, and the length guard rejects a runaway answer. So the summary you read is either the sentence the code built from counts, or a paraphrase of it; never a model's opinion of the site. Both report files are registered as artifacts and the markdown one is served by `GET /agents/forward-deployed-tester/runs/:id/report`.

examples.caption: Three pages, four findings, eleven files — the 2026-09-11 04:32 run
examples.input: `npm run agent:fdt -- --url http://127.0.0.1:4711/ --org demo-org --max-pages 5` against a local three-page demo site (home, about, contact, plus a footer link to `/missing` that answers 404). `LLM_PROVIDER=none`.
examples.output: Run `049b95fd`, status `succeeded`. `run.log`: 4 visits, 3 pages rendered (`/` 200 in 28 ms with 4 interactive elements, `/about` 200 in 12 ms with 1, `/contact` 200 in 13 ms with 4), 1 broken link, reconnaissance done in 1986 ms. 4 findings: medium broken link 404 `/missing` linked from `/`; medium 1 form with unlabeled controls on `/contact`; low 1 image without alt on `/about`; low no `<h1>` on `/about`. 11 files written to `workspace/049b95fd…/infra` — `package.json`, `playwright.config.ts`, `.mcp.json`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, `.github/workflows/playwright.yml`, `tests/fixtures.ts`, `tests/smoke.spec.ts`, `pages/HomePage.page.ts`, `pages/AboutPage.page.ts`, `pages/ContactPage.page.ts`. Executive summary: "Crawled 3 pages on http://127.0.0.1:4711 in 2.0 s (avg load 18 ms). Recorded 4 findings: 0 critical, 0 high, 2 medium, 2 low, 0 info. 1 same-origin link answered 4xx/5xx or failed to load. Provisioned a Playwright + MCP project with 3 page objects, 9 locators and 3 smoke tests."

examples.caption: How one form turns into three locators of two different qualities
examples.input: The demo contact page: `<input name="first">` with no label, no placeholder; `<label>Email <input type="email"></label>`; `<button type="submit">Send</button>`; a `Home` link.
examples.output: `pages/ContactPage.page.ts` gets four getters. `firstInput` → `page.locator("input[name=\"first\"]")` — css, medium: the harvest found no accessible name, so `deriveLocator` fell past role, label, placeholder, text and test id to the `name` attribute. `emailInput` → `page.getByRole("textbox", { name: "Email", exact: true })` — role, high: the wrapping `<label>` gave it a name and `type=email` gave it the `textbox` role. `sendButton` → `getByRole("button", { name: "Send" })` and `homeLink` → `getByRole("link", { name: "Home" })`, both high. The same unlabeled control also produced the medium accessibility finding "1 form with unlabeled controls on /contact — 1 control lack a <label>, aria-label or placeholder; screen readers and getByLabel() cannot target them". The report's locator inventory reads 8 role, 1 css.

examples.caption: A 404 in the footer becomes a finding, not a crash — and not a page
examples.input: The home page links to `/missing`. The server answers 404 with an HTML error page.
examples.output: `visit()` sees `response.status() === 404` and returns `{ broken: { url, status: 404, referrer: "http://127.0.0.1:4711/" } }` before the harvest runs, so the error page is not catalogued, gets no page object and no smoke test — the suite has 3 tests, not 4. The visit does not count against `max_pages`. `deriveFindings` emits a medium `broken-link` finding with the referrer in `detail` and the whole record in `evidence_json`. `report.md` gets a "Broken links" table (`/missing | 404 | http://127.0.0.1:4711/`). Had the link pointed at a host that does not resolve, the same path would have produced `status: 0` and a high `navigation` finding with the first line of the Playwright error.

underHood.heading: Queue and budgets
underHood.output: A `CrawlResult`: rendered `pages`, `brokenLinks`, `skipped` URLs and `durationMs` — via `crawl()`, with `normaliseUrl()` and `isCrawlable()` guarding the queue.

underHood.heading: In-page harvest
underHood.whenRuns: Inside every successful visit, after `load` and up to 2 s of network idle.
underHood.output: A `HarvestResult`: title, h1, landmark flag, alt and label counts, element counts, same-origin link list and up to 60 `ElementDescriptor`s — via `HARVEST_SCRIPT`, plain JavaScript evaluated by Playwright.

underHood.heading: Locator derivation
underHood.whenRuns: Back in Node, for every harvested descriptor.
underHood.input: Tag, type, role, accessible name, label, placeholder, text, test id, id, name attribute, classes.
underHood.output: A `DerivedLocator` with strategy, Playwright code and confidence, plus a unique camelCase property name — via `deriveLocator()`, `toPropertyName()` and `uniqueNames()`.

underHood.heading: Findings
underHood.whenRuns: Phase 2, after the crawl, before anything is written.
underHood.output: Rows in the `findings` table with severity, category, title, detail and evidence JSON — via `deriveFindings()` and `Db.addFinding()`.

underHood.heading: Provisioning and persistence
underHood.input: The page records and the run options.
underHood.output: 11+ files under `workspace/<run_id>/infra`, one `artifacts` row each; `report.md` and `report.json`; `run.log` with a timestamp per line; the `runs` row marked `succeeded` with the output JSON — via `generateInfra()`, `renderReportMarkdown()`, `buildReportJson()` and `executeAgent()`.

underHood.heading: Optional local model
underHood.whenRuns: Only in phase 4, only if a local server answers within 800 ms.
underHood.input: The deterministic summary and a prompt that forbids new facts.
underHood.output: A rephrased summary, or the original — via `maybeLlm()`; `assertLocalEndpoint()` rejects any host that is not loopback, RFC 1918 or `.local` unless `LLM_ALLOW_REMOTE=1`.

prerequisites: Node 24 (the built-in `node:sqlite` driver needs it; `npm test` passes `--experimental-sqlite`).
A clone of the repo and `npm install` — this pulls Playwright, Fastify and zod; nothing else.
Any running web app you are allowed to crawl. The agent only follows same-origin links and never submits a form.

steps.label: Install and fetch a browser
steps.cmd:
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
steps.why: The crawler launches Chromium through Playwright. Only Chromium is needed for the agent itself; the generated project installs all three engines later with `--with-deps`.
steps.firstRun: Done on 2026-09-11 while building the repo.

steps.label: Create the database
steps.why: Creates `data/forward-qa.db` with the `engagements`, `runs`, `findings` and `artifacts` tables (WAL mode, foreign keys on). Idempotent: every `CREATE TABLE` is `IF NOT EXISTS`, and every agent run calls the same schema on open anyway.
steps.rerun: Safe to repeat; nothing is dropped.

steps.label: Run it against a URL
steps.cmd:
LLM_PROVIDER=none npm run agent:fdt -- --url https://app.example.test --org acme --max-pages 10

# behind basic auth, or with a session cookie
npm run agent:fdt -- --url https://staging.example.test --org acme --basic-user qa --basic-pass secret
npm run agent:fdt -- --url https://app.example.test --org acme --cookie "session=abc123" --cookie-domain app.example.test
steps.why: The CLI creates an engagement, runs the agent and prints the output JSON (`pages_crawled`, `findings_by_severity`, `infra_dir`, `report_path`, `locators_total`, `summary`) plus the run id. `LLM_PROVIDER=none` makes the run reproducible; leave it unset and the adapter probes for a local Ollama.
steps.firstRun: 2026-09-11 04:32 against a local three-page site: 3 pages, 4 findings, 9 locators, 11 files, 2.0 s.
steps.rerun: A new run id, a new `workspace/<run_id>/` directory and new rows; earlier runs are never modified.

steps.label: Read the report
steps.why: `report.md` has the executive summary, the crawl table, broken links, findings by severity, the locator inventory per page (property, Playwright expression, confidence), the provisioned file list and five next steps. `run.log` has one timestamped line per phase and per visit.

steps.label: Run what it built
steps.cmd:
cd workspace/<run_id>/infra
npm install
npx playwright install --with-deps
npm test
BASE_URL=https://staging.example.test npm test
steps.why: The smoke suite should be green on the first run against the same environment; a red test is either a real regression or one of the findings above. `BASE_URL` overrides the baked-in target so the same suite runs against staging.
steps.firstRun: The demo run's `/about` test carries a `NOTE` instead of an h1 assertion because recon found no heading.

steps.label: Same thing through the REST API
steps.cmd:
npm start   # http://localhost:8787
curl -s -X POST localhost:8787/engagements -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"org":"acme","name":"first pass","target_url":"https://app.example.test"}'
curl -s -X POST localhost:8787/agents/forward-deployed-tester/runs -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"engagement_id":"<id>","input":{"target_url":"https://app.example.test","org_slug":"acme","max_pages":10}}'
curl -s localhost:8787/agents/forward-deployed-tester/runs/<run_id>/report
steps.why: The run is synchronous: the POST returns `{ run, output }` when the crawl is done. `GET /runs/:id` returns the run with its findings and artifacts; the report route serves `report.md` as `text/markdown`. Invalid input comes back as 400 with zod issues.

steps.label: Hand the MCP config to a client
steps.cmd:
cd workspace/<run_id>/infra
cat .mcp.json
npm run mcp    # or let Claude Code / Cursor launch it from .mcp.json
steps.why: `.mcp.json` registers the Playwright MCP server with `BASE_URL` set to the crawled site. An MCP client can open the app, walk the page objects and write new specs; the README in the generated project lists three prompts to start with.

steps.label: Run the agent's own tests
steps.why: 89 tests across both agents. For this one: locator derivation, findings rules, generators and report rendering run without a browser; `integration.test.ts` starts an in-process HTTP server and drives the real crawler through Chromium.

inputs.name: --url / target_url
inputs.desc: Start page; the crawl never leaves its origin.

inputs.name: --org / org_slug
inputs.desc: Letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Names the generated package (`<org>-e2e`) and the report.

inputs.name: --basic-user + --basic-pass, or --cookie + --cookie-domain
inputs.desc: Optional auth. Cookies are `name=value;name2=value2`; the domain defaults to the target host.

inputs.name: --headed, --no-mcp
inputs.desc: Watch the browser; skip the MCP files.

outputs.name: workspace/<run_id>/infra/
outputs.desc: The provisioned Playwright + MCP project: 8 fixed files plus one page object per page.

outputs.name: workspace/<run_id>/report.md and report.json
outputs.desc: Human and machine forms of the same report.

runbook.rerun: Nothing is cached and nothing is overwritten: every run gets a fresh run id, workspace directory and rows. Re-run after a deploy and diff the two `report.json` files — new broken links, new console errors and a changed locator inventory are the regression signal before the smoke suite even runs. Raise `max_pages` when the report says links were skipped.
runbook.integrate: Commit `workspace/<run_id>/infra` into the application repository as its `e2e/` folder; the included workflow runs on push, pull request, nightly and manual dispatch and uploads the HTML report. Point `BASE_URL` at each environment through repository variables. For the wider engagement, this run is the Discover-phase surface probe on the [process page](../process.html): its findings and the smoke suite are the baseline that later phases measure against. To add a probe of your own (an API probe, a log probe) follow the same shape — a pure `derive*()` function, rows through `ctx.db`, files through `generateInfra`-style string builders — and register it in `src/api/server.ts`.
